extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals, small businesses, comms teams seeking local TV news coverage
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for shooting, selecting, packaging, and delivering B-roll that local TV news stations will use to increase a company's broadcast coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use B-roll to garner TV news airtime
rubrics_metrics.description: B-roll is an age-old technique you can implement to garner prized airtime for your company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page cites a recent example where WTVR CBS 6 ran a story using only B-roll footage provided by the agency — demonstrating that supplying usable footage can directly lead to coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get the right equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: You don’t have to have a $5,000 or $10,000 video camera to shoot B-roll that TV news stations will use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smartphones (iPhones) often suffice, but you should invest in a tripod, lighting and a microphone. These aren’t high-dollar tools, but they ensure good quality B-roll that is more likely to be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep it simple — segment length
rubrics_metrics.description: Start and stop filming in segments of 15 to 30 seconds, but don’t do too many, which can make it hard to sort through hours and hours of video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short, focused segments make reviewing and editing easier for producers; avoid producing excessive, long unbroken takes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shoot unique, attention-getting images
rubrics_metrics.description: Think outside of the box for unique images that will get a TV producers’ attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek visually interesting shots and techniques; the author recommends learning ideas from videography resources (e.g., vlogger Peter McKinnon's tutorials) to improve cinematography and get standout B-roll.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select only a few curated clips for distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Pick three to four clips that are a maximum of 15 to 20 seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don’t overthink what you give stations — 15 seconds is a long time for news coverage. Curating a small set of ready-to-use clips increases the chance producers will use your footage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package and deliver files simply
rubrics_metrics.description: Save the clips into Dropbox or Google Drive and share the file via email with reporters or producers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use common cloud-sharing methods and a direct email to the reporter/producer so they can easily download and ingest the clips into their workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide context: short script plus press release
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a short script that an anchor could read on-air or a producer could re-write, and include your press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even excellent B-roll needs context to be used; supplying a ready-to-read script and the press release gives producers the facts and narrative to pair with footage, increasing usability.
